metadata.method_name: Bench route test of prompt bans (CRN KV-splice arms, one-shot veto, prefill) in Qwen3-8B
metadata.decoding: T=1.0, top-p 1.0, no top-k, max 1024 new tokens, CRN inverse-CDF sampling
metadata.hardware: 1 x NVIDIA L4 23 GB, 6 CPUs, 66 GB RAM
metadata.baselines: arm a (full ban) and arm b (token-length-matched neutral twin) in the same pipeline with the same uniforms; placebo splice and knockout-mechanics controls

mixed_glm.note: descriptive sensitivity (variational Bayes); logit-scale fixed effects at zero random effects

C2c.rule: SUPPORTED if hit fraction >= 2/3 AND rho < 0 with permutation p < 0.05; DISCONFIRMED if rho >= 0 or hit fraction < 1/2; else INCONCLUSIVE (committed in commit #1)

lp_readout.note: descriptive companion readout (teacher-forced log-prob of the default's signature prefix)

deviations.what: Hardware: one NVIDIA L4 (23 GB; about a third of the RTX 4090's memory bandwidth) instead of the planned RTX A4500. Measured decode latency was 89 ms/step at B=20 and 101 ms/step at B=40, so batches are B=40 rows instead of B=10.
deviations.consequence: Batch shape is constant within each shape class (task, cache length, first position); CRN partners of a slot always meet identical kernels (U1 = 1.00, U2 = 1.00).

deviations.what: Rows of different templates with equal prompt length share a batch (cross-template packing); the last batch of a class is padded with discarded duplicate rows.
deviations.consequence: None on the estimates; rows never interact inside a batch.

deviations.what: V1 (one-shot veto) runs at N=100 (k 0-19) instead of N=50; VP (persistent veto) at N=100 on the path screen; route arms c/d also run on non-gated tasks at N=100 (descriptive, Q5 upgraded).
deviations.consequence: More precision at no extra batch cost (B=40 pairs b with V1, a with c, etc.).

deviations.what: K0 is implemented by removing the condition span [p0, p1) from the cache instead of masking it (keys keep their RoPE rotation; generated queries keep positions P + step).
deviations.consequence: Exact for every generated query; checked in U3 against exp8's masked knockout (TV distance 1.2e-7 on the first generated position; eager attention mass on the span exactly 0 in all 36 layers). Lets every batch run stock SDPA with native GQA.

deviations.what: A row stops once its first fenced code block is closed (both labellers extract exactly that block).
Memory guard: finished rows are pruned from a batch once it passes step 560 (B=40 would otherwise exceed the L4's memory at ~600 new tokens).
deviations.consequence: Only rows still running past step 560 change batch shape after that step; their CRN coupling is approximate after it (logged per row as pruned_at).

deviations.what: Order: the ban-free arms (S4 b/V1, path screen round 1, twin-only controls pl/bB/K0b) ran before the analysis code was appended to commit #1, and before the T2 engine tests U1-U3/U9; no ban prompt of any task was sampled before commit #1 closed (asserted in code).
deviations.consequence: The decision rules and thresholds were already frozen in predictions/prereg.md (commit #1, first lines); the analysis code itself was committed after ban-free outputs existed.

deviations.what: Placebo splice (pl vs b under noun B) and K0b ran on the first three Stage-A tasks (T03, T04, T06) before the gate was known (the plan says the first three GATED tasks).
deviations.consequence: They are splice- and knockout-mechanics controls, valid whatever the gate.

deviations.what: Judge: the frozen bench judge j1 (gemini-2.5-flash-lite) hit transient HTTP 429 limits; failed calls are retried with backoff and rows left 'disputed' are re-judged when the label worker is idle (corrected rows appended; readers take the last row per uid). Caps: USD 0.15 per judge family (bench j1 + exp8 suite judge), total <= USD 0.30.
deviations.consequence: Rows still disputed at the end are excluded from shares (F7) and reported.

deviations.what: Proximity uses Zhang-Shasha (zss) on AST trees whose node labels are node types (user identifiers normalised; attribute names and constant types kept).
deviations.consequence: Used only in the secondary C1 rows.

deviations.what: U4-U6 (veto prefix identity, persistent-veto absence, prefill verbatim) are checked on all production rows by audit/rederive.py rather than on a separate 20-slot test.

Label-worker restarts (to add judge retries and lower the judge caps) killed the wrapper subshell instead of the Python process, so from 18:50 to 20:16 UTC up to three label workers ran concurrently and each labelled the same rows. data/samples.jsonl therefore accumulated duplicate rows (24,924 lines for 13,030 uids); it was compacted to the last row per uid, which is the row every reader (GPU queue, commit #2, analysis, audit) used throughout.
deviations.consequence: Labels come from the same frozen labellers with code-hash caches, so duplicates agree up to judge nondeterminism on a few judge-labelled programs; the audit re-derives commit #2's V_t within 0.02 and finds 0 mismatches. Some judge calls were duplicated; total judge spend stayed at USD 0.105.

deviations.what: The bench pilot was generated with Qwen3-8B-FP8 in vLLM; this artifact samples bf16 weights in HF transformers (as planned).
deviations.consequence: Arm-b default shares are 0.95 (T03), 0.76 (R6), 0.92 (T14) instead of the pilot's ~1.0; the distinctive n-gram was frozen on the pilot programs.

prereg_amendments.change: iter2_ban_landings(): recount exp12's fresh-pool landings from exp12's per-row labels (same frozen exp8/exp1 suite labeller) instead of re-judging the 200 raw texts; add a judge-free mechanical relabel as a cross-check; add BRT_SKIP_SCREEN switch for partial runs.
prereg_amendments.reason: judge budget (the suite judge costs ~USD 0.002/call); descriptive screen reference only -- no decision rule, threshold or primary statistic changed
prereg_amendments.what_had_been_seen: ban-free S4 summaries, the first path-screen rows and the T2 engine-validation counts (U9); bench ban-arm rows existed on disk but no bench ban-arm statistic had been computed

prereg_amendments.change: route_analysis(): implement the plan's pre-registered fallback F5 (3-5 gated tasks -> pooled estimate labelled low-cluster with the leave-one-task-out jackknife CI as primary); percentile and BCa verdicts still reported
prereg_amendments.reason: the gate admitted 5 tasks; the committed code computed all three intervals but hard-wired the percentile one as primary
prereg_amendments.what_had_been_seen: descriptive per-task F values of a partial smoke run (tasks T03-T06, T10) and the gate result; no pooled statistic or C2a verdict had been computed. The switch is decided solely by the number of gated tasks, as pre-registered in F5.

prereg_amendments.change: c1_rows(): a family with tied maximal probability (LADDER, scored uniform by the plan) gets top1 = null instead of the first category in catalogue order
prereg_amendments.reason: bug fix in the secondary C1 rows (no decision is made from them); the uniform LADDER previously scored spurious top-1 hits
